text: I wholeheartedly believe that in order for a relationship to last, the man needs to look at his woman and go, I can't pull any better. And I know that sounds crazy, but when he looks at his woman and goes, yep, I've reached peak, bam, that part of my life is checked off. That's the most successful relationship. That's the relationship that turns into marriage. This is one of those pieces of dating advice that sounds deep, but completely collapses when you think about it for more than five seconds. He says the most successful relationship is when a man looks at his woman and thinks, I can't pull any better. No, that mindset comes from weakness and leads to fear. A healthy relationship is not built on the belief that you reach the maximum you're capable of. It's built on choice. Big difference. Objectively speaking, there will always be women in the world who are younger, prettier, more feminine, more exciting. That's reality. But a strong man doesn't stay because he believes he can do better. He stays because he chooses his woman. When a man believes, this is the best I can get, he enters the relationship from a position of weakness, position of scarcity. And scarcity creates fear, fear of loss, fear of replacement, fear of abandonment. And that fear completely ruins the power dynamic. A man who is afraid of losing his woman will tolerate behavior he shouldn't tolerate. He'll avoid voicing his opinion. He will overinvest. He will suppress boundaries. And women feel this. And once a woman feels that a man settled out of insecurity, attraction gradually dies. Respect disappears. A much better approach to life is to choose a woman from a position of abundance. That's when, as a man, you have experience, you have options, and you know that if your relationship ends tomorrow, your life doesn't collapse. You've worked on yourself and you continue to work on yourself. So you live your life, you meet women, and then you meet one who actually fits your criteria. You choose this woman not because you can't pull any better, but because she fits your values, your standards, your lifestyle. That makes commitment stable instead of desperate. And the same logic applies in reverse. A woman should choose you not because she's afraid she won't find better, but because you meet her criteria as a man. That's how good, healthy relationships work. Not through fear of loss, but through mutual, conscious choice.
